name: Swansea University

settingEvidence.evidence: Swansea University spans two stunning campuses at each end of Swansea’s waterfront.

fees.text: £9,790 per year for UK (Home) students starting in September 2027 (2027/28), the same as the 2026/27 fee. Swansea says any future Welsh Government fee changes (such as inflation-linked rises) will be reflected in what it charges. A Year Abroad is charged at 15% and a Year in Industry at 20% of the standard fee.

livingCosts.text: University halls cost £130–£258 a week depending on the room (average £185 a week, about £7,400 for a 40-week contract, for a medium en-suite); utilities, internet and contents insurance are included and a £100 reservation deposit is payable (2026/27). A room in a private shared house averages about £122 a week rent plus about £16 a week bills.

source.evidence: University accommodation costs range from £130 per week - £258 per week depending on requirements

events.label: Undergraduate open day (Singleton Park and Bay campuses)

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 7 November 2026 (registration from 8:30am to about 4pm on both campuses; book in advance). Spring open days are mentioned but their dates aren't published yet. Online 'Masterclass Series' course webinars run in Autumn 2026.

source.evidence: Sign up for our next open day 7th November

contextual.summary: Swansea doesn't publish a general contextual-offer scheme with criteria for these courses; its admissions policy says finishing its Step Up programme, or being a care leaver, may lead to a reduced offer (the size of the reduction isn't stated).
contextual.typicalReduction: A tariff point reduction / reduced offer (amount not stated on the pages checked)

criteria.detail: Successfully completing the Step Up to Swansea University programme (for first-year A-Level/BTEC students at schools and colleges in South West Wales) may lead to a reduced offer for certain undergraduate programmes. Applicants who completed a similar compact or summer school at another university can send full details to the Admissions Office to ask for the same points reduction.
Students who have been in care for more than 3 months and have a Care Leavers' Pathway Plan get a support package that may lead to a reduced offer.

contextual.rulesText: Swansea says each application is still considered on its merits. Successful completion of the Step Up programme may lead to a reduced offer for certain undergraduate programmes, and the care-leaver support package may lead to a reduced offer. No other contextual criteria or grade reductions are published on the pages checked.

source.evidence: Successful completion of the Step Up programme may lead to a reduced offer

programmes.name: Step Up to Swansea University
programmes.summary: A series of day events (information, guidance and subject taster days) plus a short summer school for first-year A-Level and BTEC students from under-represented backgrounds in South West Wales, with a tariff point reduction for Swansea courses if you complete it.
programmes.whoCanApply: First-year A-Level and BTEC students from backgrounds under-represented in higher education, including young carers, care experienced young people and young people living in the lower 40% of the Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation. Swansea says the Step Up team can only work with schools and colleges in South West Wales, so students elsewhere (for example Bournemouth) are pointed to the Swansea Recruitment Team instead.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: A targeted programme for students from backgrounds under-represented in higher education, 'including, but not limited to' young carers, care experienced young people, and young people living in areas in the lower 40% of the Welsh Index of Multiple Deprivation. Only schools and colleges in South West Wales are supported. Students apply individually; selection is in February and students are told by early March.
benefits: Tariff point reduction for Swansea University courses if you successfully complete the programme (size not stated)

programmes.name: Swansea University Undergraduate Summer School
programmes.summary: A July summer school for Year 12 students with a 3-day residential (or day passes) of hands-on workshops in courses including Business, Law, Medicine and Engineering.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students curious about university life or considering a degree. Applications are reviewed after the deadline, so a place isn't automatic.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Open to Year 12 students; financial assistance may be offered to successful UK applicants if the cost is a barrier.

notes: No 2028-entry pages yet: the course pages list September 2027 starts (and January 2028 for January-start versions), so all courses use 2027 entry.

Swansea's BSc Economics page says all Economics programmes will be taught at Bay Campus (SA1 8EN) from September 2027 (the Economics, Economics and Finance and Economics and Business key-details boxes still say Singleton Park Campus). Accounting and Finance, Finance and Business Management are taught at Bay Campus; the PPE page lists Singleton Park Campus (SA2 8PP).
Swansea is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and no course page names an admissions test.
Swansea says it guarantees a conditional offer to every UK undergraduate applicant studying the qualifications required for their chosen course (not professional courses).
Swansea says that if you obtain grades AAA-AAB or equivalent you qualify for an Excellence or Merit Scholarship.
Swansea says applicants predicted grade B or above in an EPQ get an offer one grade lower, e.g. AAB becomes ABB plus EPQ B.
The year of the 7 November open day (2026) is shown on Swansea's booking page (tickettailor.com/events/swanseauniversity1/2339398); the swansea.ac.uk open days page only says '7th November'.

competition: Swansea doesn't publish offer rates or applications per place on its course pages
